runs.name: Health element and PIP removal for young people, from April 2027 (combined)
runs.description: The health element removal for under-25s (all claimants) and the PIP removal for 18 to 24-year-olds simulated together, with their interactions.

runs.name: Health element removal with severe cases kept and PIP at half rate, from April 2027 (combined)
runs.description: The health element removal for under-25s with severe cases kept, and PIP at half rate for 18 to 24-year-olds in place of a new additional cost allowance, simulated together with their interactions.
runs.reason: It keeps the health element for claimants with 24 or more PIP daily living points, which the calculator does not ask for.

runs.name: UC health element removed for under-25s
runs.description: From April 2027 Universal Credit awards no longer include the health (LCWRA) element where the claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity is under 25, for existing and new claimants alike; an award keeps it where a joint claimant aged 25 or over has that capability. The assessment itself is unchanged, so the work allowance still applies, but an award without the element loses the benefit cap exception that rests on it.

runs.name: UC health element removed for under-25 new claims
runs.description: From April 2027 Universal Credit awards paid the health element at the new-claimant rate (claims from April 2026) no longer include it where the claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity is under 25; protected claimants keep it. The data store an ordering of claims by the survey's Universal Credit start date, then age: the model gives the new-claimant rate to the most recent claims at the expected share each year, so the figure rests on that ordering.

runs.name: PIP removed for 18 to 24-year-olds
runs.description: From April 2027 people aged 18 to 24 receive neither component of Personal Independence Payment; 16 and 17-year-olds keep it and Disability Living Allowance for children is unchanged. Universal Credit amounts that depend on receiving PIP go with it; Carer's Allowance is not linked to PIP in the model and does not change. Scottish recipients of Adult Disability Payment, which the data record as PIP, are included.

runs.name: Under-25 UC standard allowance at the 25-and-over rate
runs.description: From April 2027 single Universal Credit claimants under 25 receive the standard allowance for those aged 25 and over, and couples in which both are under 25 receive the couple rate for those aged 25 and over. The protected health element is held at its current-law amount, which the law otherwise links to the under-25 allowances. The report proposes a Youth Allowance at the under-25 rate, higher only for those living independently; this run shows the higher rate for every under-25.

runs.name: Employer NICs zero rate extended to under-25s
runs.description: From April 2027 employers pay no Class 1 National Insurance on earnings up to the upper secondary threshold (£50,270 a year) for employees under 25, extending the zero rate for under-21s. The model passes employers' National Insurance through to wages, so the saving shows as higher pay for these employees. The report considers this option and does not propose it (paragraph 268); it proposes a higher threshold for 21 to 24-year-olds in retail and hospitality instead.
runs.note: The model passes the employer's saving to pay.

runs.name: UC health element removed for under-22s
runs.description: From April 2027 Universal Credit awards no longer include the health (LCWRA) element where the claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity is under 22, for existing and new claimants alike: the age limit proposed in the 2025 Pathways to Work green paper.

runs.name: UC health element removed for under-25s, severe cases kept
runs.description: As the removal for under-25s, except that a young claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity who scores 24 or more PIP daily living points (about a fifth of young PIP recipients) keeps the element. The points stand in for the report's Severe and Complex Needs Insurance, for which the report gives no eligibility test.
runs.reason: It keeps the health element for claimants with 24 or more PIP daily living points, which the calculator does not ask for.

runs.name: PIP at half rate for 18 to 24-year-olds
runs.description: From April 2027 people aged 18 to 24 receive half their current Personal Independence Payment. This is an illustrative stand-in for the report's Additional Cost Allowance, for which the report gives no rates; Scottish Adult Disability Payment, recorded as PIP, is included. Half an award can fall below the amounts that some disability rules read, such as severe disability status, so those can be lost too; a new allowance could carry its own qualifying rules. Carer's Allowance is not linked to PIP in the model and does not change.

runs.name: PIP removed for 16 to 24-year-olds
runs.description: As the PIP removal for 18 to 24-year-olds, but from age 16: 'under 25' read literally. Disability Living Allowance for children under 16 is unchanged.

runs.name: Health element and PIP removal from April 2027, phased as claimants are reassessed
runs.description: The health element and PIP removals for young people, reaching people who turned 18 since April 2026 at once, and existing claimants as they are reassessed, at an assumed 25% of those remaining each year. Who is reassessed is a random draw, as the data hold no reassessment dates.
runs.reason: Who is reassessed each year is a random draw across the population, so one household's result would be that draw, not the policy.

runs.name: Health element and PIP removal from April 2027, with an illustrative move into work
runs.description: The full package, with a randomly chosen quarter of affected young people who do not work (aged 18 to 24, with PIP or limited capability for work and work-related activity) moving into 16 hours a week at their minimum wage. An illustrative scenario, not an estimate of how people would respond.
runs.reason: An illustrative move into work for a random quarter of affected young people: one household's result would be that draw, not the policy.

runs.name: Health element and PIP removal for young people, from April 2029 (combined)
runs.description: Two of the report's benefit changes, simulated together with their interactions and without its replacement payments: UC health element removed for under-25s; PIP removed for 18 to 24-year-olds. The report's other modelled measures, such as the higher Youth Allowance, are separate runs.

runs.name: UC health element removed for under-25s
runs.description: From April 2029 Universal Credit awards no longer include the health (LCWRA) element where the claimant with limited capability for work and work-related activity is under 25, for existing and new claimants alike; an award keeps it where a joint claimant aged 25 or over has that capability. The assessment itself is unchanged, so the work allowance still applies, but an award without the element loses the benefit cap exception that rests on it.

runs.name: PIP removed for 18 to 24-year-olds
runs.description: From April 2029 people aged 18 to 24 receive neither component of Personal Independence Payment; 16 and 17-year-olds keep it and Disability Living Allowance for children is unchanged. Universal Credit amounts that depend on receiving PIP go with it; Carer's Allowance is not linked to PIP in the model and does not change. Scottish recipients of Adult Disability Payment, which the data record as PIP, are included.

runs.name: Employer NI threshold of £10,000 for 21 to 24s in retail and hospitality
runs.description: The report's end state: employers pay Class 1 National Insurance on earnings above £10,000 a year, not £5,000, for employees aged 21 to 24 whose main job is in retail (SIC division 47) or hospitality (divisions 55 and 56). The 15% rate is unchanged, and under-21s and apprentices under 25 keep their zero rate. The report gives no start date or costing and proposes a five-year glide path; the end state is shown in every year. policyengine-uk holds each employer's total cost of employment fixed, so the saving passes to employees as higher pay; hiring does not respond.
runs.note: The threshold applies to 21 to 24-year-olds in retail and hospitality; the model passes the employer's saving to pay.

runs.name: Higher Youth Allowance for under-25s living independently
runs.description: From April 2029 Universal Credit claims in which every adult is under 25 and that include a housing costs element are paid the standard allowance for those aged 25 and over, the review's own proxy for living independently (analytical annex, section 8). Other young claims keep the under-25 rate, which the report proposes as the Youth Allowance's base level. The report gives no amount for its work allowance, so none is modelled.

runs.name: Health element and PIP removal from April 2029, phased as claimants are reassessed
runs.description: The report's health element and PIP changes for young people, reaching people who turned 18 since April 2028 at once, and existing claimants as they are reassessed, at an assumed 45% of those remaining each year. Who is reassessed is a random draw, as the data hold no reassessment dates.
runs.reason: Who is reassessed each year is a random draw across the population, so one household's result would be that draw, not the policy.

runs.name: Employer NI threshold for 21 to 24s in retail and hospitality, phased in
runs.description: The report's five-year glide path, in assumed equal steps from April 2027: the employer National Insurance threshold for employees aged 21 to 24 whose main job is in retail (SIC 47) or hospitality (SIC 55 and 56) is £6,000 in 2027-28, rising £1,000 a year to £10,000 in 2031-32. The report gives no start date or steps. The 15% rate is unchanged; the saving passes to pay.
runs.note: In 2029-30 the glide path's threshold is £8,000, its third step (the end state, £10,000, is reached in 2031-32).

runs.name: Work allowance for under-25s in work (illustrative)
runs.description: From April 2029 every Universal Credit claim in which all claimants are under 25 has a work allowance: earnings below it do not reduce the award. The report proposes a work allowance for everyone on the Youth Allowance who is in employment (para 749) and gives no amount. The amount here is our assumption: the current Universal Credit work allowance, the lower rate for claims with a housing costs element and the higher rate for those without, uprated each year. Claims that already have a work allowance (with a child or limited capability for work) keep it, and the 55% taper and the standard allowance are unchanged.

runs.name: Higher Youth Allowance and work allowance (illustrative) for under-25s, from April 2029 (combined)
runs.description: Our combination of two of the report's Youth Allowance proposals, simulated together with their interactions: the 25-and-over standard allowance for under-25 claims with a housing costs element (the review's proxy for living independently), and a work allowance for every Universal Credit claim in which all claimants are under 25. The report gives no work allowance amount; the current Universal Credit work allowance is our assumption, so the run is illustrative.

runs.name: Health element and PIP removal with higher Youth Allowance and work allowance (illustrative), from April 2029 (combined)
runs.description: Our combination, simulated together with their interactions: UC health element removed for under-25s; PIP removed for 18 to 24-year-olds; the higher Youth Allowance for under-25s living independently; and the illustrative work allowance for under-25s (the current Universal Credit work allowance, our assumption: the report gives no amount). The report's replacement payments are not modelled.

runs.name: Employer NI threshold of £10,000 for all 21 to 24s (illustrative)
runs.description: Illustrative: the report's end state extended to every sector. Employers pay Class 1 National Insurance on earnings above £10,000 a year, not £5,000, for every employee aged 21 to 24, whatever the sector. The report starts with retail and hospitality and says the government should consider extending the relief to other sectors over time (para 270), naming none; every sector, from April 2027, is our assumption. The 15% rate is unchanged, and under-21s and apprentices under 25 keep their zero rate. policyengine-uk holds each employer's total cost of employment fixed, so the saving passes to employees as higher pay; hiring does not respond.
runs.note: The threshold applies to 21 to 24-year-olds in every sector; the model passes the employer's saving to pay.

runs.name: Work allowance at 15 hours' minimum-wage pay (illustrative)
runs.description: From April 2029 every Universal Credit claim in which all claimants are under 25 has a work allowance of 15 hours a week at the minimum wage for workers aged 21 and over, over 52 weeks, a month (about £900 in 2029-30): earnings below it do not reduce the award. The report proposes a work allowance for everyone on the Youth Allowance who is in employment and says many young people out of work could work 10 or 15 hours a week at first (para 749); it gives no amount. The amount is our assumption, the same with or without a housing costs element. Claims with a work allowance today (with a child or limited capability for work) get the higher of the two. The 55% taper and the standard allowance are unchanged.

assumptions.text: The examples rent privately at £500 a month, in the North West.
Living with parents counts as a household of one with no rent: the parents' income, housing costs and TV licence are left out.
Council Tax and Council Tax Reduction are left out.
2029-30 benefit rates, minimum wage and tax thresholds, on the OBR forecast; every award is claimed in full, all year.
The report's replacement payments are not modelled: nothing is paid in place of the health element or PIP.
Each run is compared with current law on its own; runs are never added together.
Losing PIP daily living can move a single renter under 35 to the shared accommodation rate, so the Universal Credit housing element falls too.
Hours, wages and housing costs are held fixed (the employer National Insurance saving is passed to pay); no behavioural response.
